newsitem.title: GERMANY: German officials seize beef, suspect ban breach.
newsitem.headline: German officials seize beef, suspect ban breach.

text.p: German officials said on Monday they had seized a cargo of beef from Belgium which they believed was British meat exported illegally in defiance of a worldwide export ban.
The agriculture ministry in the northern state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern said the meat had been seized at the port of Mukran on the island of Ruegen at the weekend.
"The meat in question is part of the goods which hit the headlines a few days ago," the ministry said in a statement. "British meat was to have been relabelled and falsely declared."
The ministry did not say how large the cargo of meat had been. It said the load would have passed through Germany as a transit country en route for Russia.
"There was no danger at any stage of this meat reaching the German market," the statement said.
The European Commission said last week that 1,600 tonnes of British beef had been exported illegally, with Belgian help, to the Netherlands, Russia and Egypt despite the mad cow crisis.
The export ban was imposed in March 1996 after the British government admitted a likely link between mad cow disease and its deadly human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease.
